newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker but locked in range.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker but locked in range.

text.p: White sugar futures held within their morning ranges in modest volume on Thursday but failed to derive much momentum or support from the lacklustre tone in New York, traders said.
A fair share of the turnover came from against actuals trades but routine business was the order of the day with very little interest reported to trade arbitrages against the raws, they said.
At 1550 GMT all traded positions had lost ground and movements were tight across the board. Volume amounted to 1,217 lots.
August was 80 cents lower at $306.20 and October down 10 cents at $302.70.
"I don't see it going crazy on the downside...I think it's going to trade within the range," said one trader.

Technically, August has skidded along $306.00 support as an intraday low for two consecutive trading sessions, reluctant to push back above the upward trendline which had been underneath the market since late January.
In other news, Alfa Group, one of Russia's biggest importers of Cuban raw sugar, is said to be considering extending a credit of up to $50 million to Cuba to help finance the 1998 sugar cane harvest.
Alfa Group was reported to be planning to import 300,000 tonnes of Cuban raws up to June.
Volume was static in Paris with very few new trades posted in the afternoon. In a total volume of 30 lots August was the only contract traded, up 50 cents at $307.50.
